edits.old: Treating a Compass schema sample as a complete data-quality audit is an anti-pattern. Sampling can omit rare fields or type variants; use targeted checks for exceptional records before concluding that they do not exist. (high confidence)

edits.old: An anti-pattern warning does not justify banning arrays. MongoDB recommends bounded subsets for some access patterns, while independent research treats a bounded order-line array as sensible and an entire customer order history as unsafe nesting. (high confidence)
edits.new: An anti-pattern warning does not justify banning arrays. MongoDB says arrays let you embed data that is accessed together, and recommends subsetting and referencing to bound arrays rather than embedding entire datasets. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/data-modeling/design-antipatterns/unbounded-arrays.md

evidence.quote: Storing arrays as field values lets you embed data and ensure that data that is accessed together is stored together.
Instead of embedding entire datasets, use subsetting and referencing to bound arrays

edits.old: Unnecessary indexes and bloated documents deserve explicit review: the vendor describes storage and write costs from excess indexes and common-query costs from large documents; the research mapping reports the same categories and working-set pressure. (high confidence)
edits.new: Unnecessary indexes and bloated documents deserve explicit review: MongoDB documents that unnecessary indexes consume additional disk space and can degrade write performance, and that bloated (excessively large) documents can degrade the performance of the most common queries, in part because the working set may no longer fit in RAM. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/data-modeling/design-antipatterns.md ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/data-modeling/design-antipatterns/bloated-documents.md

evidence.quote: Your collection contains unnecessary indexes. Unnecessary indexes consume additional disk space and can degrade write performance.
Your collection has excessively large documents. The large documents can degrade the performance of your most common queries.
However, if documents are too large, the working set might not fit into RAM, causing performance to degrade as MongoDB has to access data from disk.
